html:
SMTO-CFG-0077 — SMTO can't use your automatic Skill selection settings

GUID: c0c6b867-09e8-5ca7-8831-4de89b8a82cb
Slug: capability-selection-config-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_selection

What happened

  • Your Capabilities settings mark a Skill or tool as Always that SMTO no longer has, use a format this version doesn't understand, or differ from what a queued request saved. SMTO stopped before starting anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Capabilities (in the message box controls), find Always rules for Skills or tools you deleted or that vanished after an update. Set them to Auto, then select Apply. Always rules can only point at Skills and tools SMTO still has installed.
  2. If you can't find the bad rule, select Reset in the Capabilities window, choose your Skills again, and select Apply. Reset clears every Always rule for that Apply to level, including ones for missing Skills, but also clears your other choices there.
  3. If the message came from a queued request, remove it from the queue with its Delete queued task button and send it again as a new message. A queued request keeps the Skill settings it was queued with and can't be sent with different ones.

What success looks like

  • Your message starts a task, or Capabilities saves without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit SMTO's settings files by hand to remove the rule; use the Capabilities window so the change is checked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Capability selection configuration was rejected: schema_version is not 1, an always_skill_ids or always_tool_ids entry is not registered, or a prepared or queued submission supplied a capability_selection or capability_policy that differs from its captured snapshot (409).

What this means

  • Automatic-selection settings have an unsupported version, refer to unregistered Always IDs, or differ from an already captured queue submission's selection configuration. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Automatic-selection settings have an unsupported version, refer to unregistered Always IDs, or differ from an already captured queue submission's selection configuration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact registered IDs and whether the request is attempting to replace an immutable queued selection.

How to fix it

  • Compare the conversation and global capability_selection settings with registry.skill_ids() and tool_ids(), and remove unregistered Always IDs through the Capabilities editor or settings API. For queued work, resubmit without overriding capability_selection or capability_policy (the captured snapshot is immutable), or delete the queue item and submit new work.
  • Correct unregistered selection rules or use the captured queue configuration; use new task settings for intentionally changed selections.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Valid registered choices are accepted for new work while existing snapshots stay unchanged.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
